key_insight: Deep-learning Hessian spectra can be explained as the symmetry-broken version of a nearby highly symmetric reference model, which naturally produces zero-kernel structure, large multiplicities, and a few outlier eigenvalues.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a geometric lens for diagnosing optimization curvature and loss landscape structure across architectures such as MLPs, CNNs, GNNs, and transformers.
method: Identify a nearby reference configuration with rich invariances beyond standard weight symmetries.
Analyze how those symmetries force Hessian eigenvalue multiplicities and high-dimensional nullspaces.
Show that moving back to the trained/original setting breaks symmetry and yields the observed bulk-plus-outlier spectrum.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a detailed theoretical analysis, including three-layer ReLU networks and extensions to convolutional, graph, transformer, NTK, layerwise Hessians, and the Gauss-Newton matrix, rather than a primarily empirical benchmark study.
watch_item: The symmetry-based picture relies on constructing or approximating a nearby reference model, so practical use may depend on how well a real trained network matches that idealization.
paper_title: Eigenvalues of the Hessian in Deep Learning: The Origin of Symmetry and Its Breaking
